---
title: "Results, Reports, and Diagrams"
subtitle: "How does verified evidence become a Python-facing presentation?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `STABILIZED` Full V1 implementation; adaptive presentation-theme
semantics are a `CONVERGING` candidate.

## Separate materialized values from analysis evidence

`Result` is the shared immutable, already-materialized value role.
`AnalysisResult` is the receipt-backed terminal subset and exposes immutable
`ResultIdentity(plan_sha256, request_sha256, attempt_sha256, result_sha256)`.
`DirectSolveResult`, `DiagonalRootResult`, `OptimizationResult`, and
`HBBatchResult` derive from it. Each HB batch contains one `HBCaseOutcome` for
every declared case. The outcome is a derived view of its parent receipt: a
success exposes matrices and states; a numerical failure exposes its stored
`HBCaseFailure`. `ExplanationResult`, `CircuitDiagramResult`, and
`ReportResult` remain derived values and do not fabricate operation receipts.

## Reconstruct typed Results in Python

Python verifies the receipt and manifest before constructing an `AnalysisResult`. Scalars
and axes become SCNSim-registry Pint Quantities; matrix payloads become labeled
NumPy arrays with ordered coordinate, mode, frequency, unit, and load-state
metadata. An Analysis Result retains request, attempt, artifact, and runtime
identity even when its chunks are loaded lazily.

Direct matrix channels use `(coordinate, ())`. HB input and output channels use
flattened `(coordinate, mode)` pairs in coordinate-major/mode-minor order.
`MatrixView.input_channels` and `output_channels` expose those exact stored-axis
labels; presentation never infers a reshape or relabels a mode.

HB operating-point state arrays use the distinct structured axes
`(pump_mode, node_coordinate)`: each pump-mode label is an ordered integer
tuple in request pump-axis order, and each node-coordinate label is the sealed
compiler identity recorded by `state_node_map`. These labels are evidence, not
new View selectors or Port aliases.

The Result catalog describes artifact meaning (role, dtype, shape, axes, units,
and channel order). Its HB links carry case-local
`{case_id, id, path, sha256}` references. The accompanying manifest instead
seals the byte tree. A repeated local ID or SHA-256 across cases is valid; only
the complete reference within its receipt-bound attempt has an addressable
role.

No Result unpickles arbitrary Python objects. Missing chunks, mismatched shape,
unit disagreement, non-finite forbidden values, or a real/imag manifest mismatch
fails during verification rather than returning a partially typed object.

## Keep presentation downstream of execution

Matplotlib renders numerical `show()` surfaces. `magnitude="linear" | "db"`
transforms only the displayed S magnitude; source arrays remain unchanged.
Every theme entry accepts only the public `Theme.AUTO`, `Theme.LIGHT`, or
`Theme.DARK` enum value and raises `TypeError` before rendering for raw strings
or other values. Matplotlib still returns an actual `Figure`, Schemdraw an
actual `Drawing`, and HTML presentation its HTML object.

`Theme.AUTO` uses a light-styled object as its portable static fallback, then
supplies a self-contained SVG/HTML rich representation whose foreground and
background switch together under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`. A frontend
without media-query support therefore remains readable in light mode.
`Theme.LIGHT` and `Theme.DARK` are fixed, self-contained renderings. Calling
the existing `Drawing.save()` or `Figure.savefig()` directly preserves an
explicit theme; `AUTO` saves the light fallback for SVG and raster output.
Presentation never reads environment variables or frontend-specific state.

The light and dark palettes share one fixed paired ten-color cycle. Changing
theme cannot change source arrays, curve or case order, line count, labels,
legend, axes, diagram geometry, layout, topology, or any Plan/request/Result
identity. Styling is applied per object without changing Matplotlib `rcParams`
or Schemdraw global configuration. A Notebook or interactive frontend may
display the returned object; headless code receives it without pretending a
window opened.

| Role | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| background | `#ffffff` | `#111827` |
| foreground | `#243044` | `#eaf2fb` |
| secondary text | `#5b677a` | `#a8b7ca` |
| grid/border | `#d8e1ec` | `#2b3a4f` |
| primary accent | `#2f80d1` | `#7bb7f0` |

The paired line cycle, in order, is
`#2f80d1/#7bb7f0`, `#c76b00/#f2a65a`, `#2e7d32/#7dcc8a`,
`#7e57c2/#b39ddb`, `#c44536/#ff8a80`, `#0f766e/#2dd4bf`,
`#a16207/#facc15`, `#be185d/#f472b6`, `#0e7490/#22d3ee`, and
`#475569/#cbd5e1`. The left/right member is the light/dark rendering of the
same trace index.

Schemdraw renders authoring and compiler-expanded schematics as vector output.
Authoring diagrams are a read-only projection of a structurally complete
authored Plan; they do not seal it. Compiled diagrams consume a Julia preflight
graph and must show every declared pi section and matrix-valued block without
pretending to be a reduced or backend-result circuit.

## Assemble reports from explicit inputs

`ReportSpec.inputs` contains exact `AnalysisResult` objects already held by the
caller, and `ReportSpec.theme` selects the same strict presentation enum used
by diagrams and figures. Report assembly verifies result identities, preserves
each native grid, and records every failed outcome carried by an input HB
batch. Its HTML, tables, and embedded Direct/HB SVG use one theme; `AUTO`
adapts in the browser while explicit themes remain fixed. It does not search
the workspace, infer a latest Result, run an analysis, interpolate curves, or
decide whether a Design Target passed.

`ReportResult` is pure derived data, not a terminal operation. Its
`save(path)` accepts a new `.html` file beneath an existing parent, refuses
overwrite, writes atomically, and returns `Path`. The file is standalone and
self-contained: it embeds figures, summary tables, and complete source
identities, but excludes complete large raw arrays, workspace links,
timestamps, and inferred PASS/FAIL. Additional formats wait for a named
consumer.

Suffix, missing-parent, and existing-target checks use `ValueError`,
`FileNotFoundError`, and `FileExistsError`; other filesystem failures retain
their ordinary `OSError` subtype. Export creates no operation receipt.
